(2) Authoring: the fluent form cut the spec from 165 to 116 lines and reads as one hierarchy, but kebab-case keys force bracket-indexing on built-spec handles, so tests need a re-export block for clean names (provenance-2lg). (3) Verification: Bun still needs explicit { file: import.meta.path } on every verify call (provenance-6vo). (4) Semantic diff: a no-op plan is trustworthy, zero spurious diffs across a full restyle. (5) Install: local symlink plus PROVENANCE_BIN works but is brittle (the link pointed into a deleted Codex worktree); the installs-only-the-package criterion is unreachable while the SDK is unpublished.

Fixed in PR #111 (merged as 1d3bfee) by a mint claude-opus worker. Mechanism per ADR 0006: a verification run is desired state only for the owner, file, and key it reports; re-pointing an owner-local key in a file retires the binding it replaced in place (same Stable ID, reactivated on re-report); only declared_by retires through this path. Active coverage/wiki/stale/plan views exclude retired bindings; export/import/check/graph references keep them as history. Bindings whose file vanished surface as gone via the stale gate rather than auto-retiring. RED/GREEN recorded per behavior in the PR body; 1012 workspace tests, clippy, and all 11 CI checks green. Residual boundary, deliberate: a wrapper deleted while its file survives leaves the binding active but visibly stale (evidence file changed); presenting and disposing of that tail belongs to provenance-o1b.3's review surface.

Fixed in PR #117 (merged as 4408196) by a local claude-opus worker. Root cause was not stack format: JavaScriptCore implements proper tail calls, so test('x', () => rule.verify(key, cb)) replaces the calling frame with the callee's and the frame is never pushed; no parser can recover it. Fix: verify's options now accept import.meta itself (one optional url field on VerifyOptions), file also accepts a module URL, URL wins over file (Bun's import.meta.file is a bare basename), and the existing { file: import.meta.path } call sites work unchanged. A call that can name no file fails before the callback runs with an error naming import.meta, instead of sending nothing to Rust. Bun regression fixture runs in CI via oven-sh/setup-bun (bun-version latest, pin later if reproducibility matters more than early warning) plus a Node-side simulation. RED/GREEN recorded in the PR: Node 55/59 with four behavioral failures then 60/60; Bun 0/2 then 2/2 under real Bun 1.3.14.

Campaign complete: three representative workflowd changes implemented by claude-opus workers with Provenance upkeep required but never specified, supervisor auditing after each run without mid-run correction. VERDICT: the agent-maintenance hypothesis is SUPPORTED, 3 for 3 with zero supervisor interventions. Run 1 (vs3.14.4, Structure routing contract, PR #40): worker unprompted added requirement agent-contract-fidelity with a hash-match rule when the bundled contract became load-bearing, applied state, wired a real behavioral verification; audit found no missed or wrong updates. Run 2 (9uq refactor over evidence-carrying code, PR #41): worker correctly left the spec untouched with an argued scope rationale; audit confirmed zero evidence sites in the diff via plan and sdk stale. Run 3 (3d8 control, unrelated readiness feature, PR #42): worker again correctly refrained, grounding the call in the design doc that assigns readiness outside QRSPI scope; audit confirmed 24/24 unchanged, 0 affected. No over-booking occurred in either restraint case. Graph accuracy held across all three: independent plan, evidence, neighbors, and stale queries agreed with each worker's account. FINDINGS for the roadmap: (1) both restraint cases hinged on the spec's declared scope; a second spec/scope for non-QRSPI subsystems is the natural next modeling step and agents already reason about it correctly; (2) cited-source content changes surface only through diff-based stale with an explicit base, consistent with ADR 0007, but nothing prompts a reviewer to supply that base; (3) the boundary between contract/eval-enforced obligations and runtime-code obligations (run 1's deliberate omission) is unmodeled and needs a shaping decision; (4) dogfood CI stays permanently red while the SDK is unpublished, and the symlinked package leaks its own Node-targeted tests into bun test sweeps - both environment costs of the no-publish stance.
